Shanghai上海

The deepest market, and the one most foreign buyers inspect first.

Median asking
¥70k–140k/m²
Gross yield
1.4%–1.9%
Purchase cap
One self-use home
Land term
70 years, residential

Shanghai is where the foreign-buyer question gets asked most often, and for good reason: it has the largest resident expatriate population in mainland China, the widest choice of stock, and the most mature professional infrastructure — English-speaking counsel, bilingual notaries, banks that have processed foreign purchase files before.

It is also the most expensive and the most tightly administered. Purchase limits, tax treatment and mortgage policy are all applied at the municipal level, and the practical rules differ from what a national-level summary will tell you.

Can a foreigner buy here?

One self-use home only. You must have worked or studied in Shanghai for at least one year, and the property must be in Shanghai. Bring passport, valid residence permit, employment or enrolment proof, and a marriage certificate if applicable.

Most foreign purchases are self-use apartments in Jing'an, Xuhui, Changning and Pudong, typically 1–3 bedrooms between 90m² and 180m².

Before you view anything here

The paragraph above is a summary, not an answer. City practice is applied at district level and changes without much notice.

Take it to the counter: ask the district housing bureau to confirm your eligibility in writing, using the script in how to verify.

How to check it

Where to live

Districts that work for foreign buyers

Not every district is workable at every stage. These are the ones with the schools, services and resale liquidity foreigners actually need.

Jing'an静安

Central, walkable, strong rental demand from corporate tenants. The default choice for buyers who want the city on foot.

Xuhui徐汇

The old French Concession grid plus strong schools. Best balance of character, education and resale liquidity.

Changning长宁

Gubei and Hongqiao: the established Japanese and Korean communities, international schools, and larger family apartments.

Pudong浦东

Lujiazui for new-build towers, Jinqiao for villa compounds and international schools, Zhangjiang for tech employment.

Minhang闵行

Where families go for space and schooling. Longer commutes, better value per square metre.

The market

How Shanghai actually trades

The secondary market dominates. New-build supply inside the Outer Ring is scarce and often sold under price guidance that only appears at launch, so most foreign buyers end up in resale apartments or in villa compounds on the eastern and western edges.

Living here

Settling in

Two international airports, a metro that reaches almost everywhere, and the deepest concentration of international schools and English-speaking hospitals in the country. This is the easiest Chinese city for a newly arrived family to operate in.

Know before you offer

Three risks in this market

  • Price guidance on new launches is opaque; the advertised range is not the transacted range.
  • Older lane houses (老洋房) carry heritage restrictions that can block renovation.
  • School catchment rules change, and a confirmed place is not guaranteed by proximity alone.

Best suited to

Buyers who need depth of choice, professional infrastructure and liquidity on exit.
